bugs: Marking a task done without also setting completed_at (e.g. $task->update(['status' => 'done'])) means it never shows up in tasks_completed_last_7_days. Nothing keeps status and completed_at consistent, and completed_at is mass-assignable (app/Models/Task.php:17). Probe confirmed this.

The API endpoints are registered in routes/web.php:11-14 under an 'api' prefix, so they run the full web stack (sessions, cookies, CSRF). The probe showed session cookies being set on /api/exchange-rates responses.
A request that waits on the refresh lock blocks for up to lock_wait=5s (config/services.php) before falling back to stale data, which is longer than the 3s 'slow API' budget (probe: 4.9s).
antipatterns: routes/web.php:11 — API routes placed in web.php with Route::prefix('api') instead of routes/api.php plus withRouting(api:)

app/Services/ExchangeRates.php:27 — catches the broad RuntimeException as control flow; refresh() throws RuntimeException to signal 'down' and rewraps ConnectionException (line 59), so unrelated RuntimeExceptions are swallowed as well
app/Services/ExchangeRates.php:40-41 — multi-line comment that restates what the code does
config/services.php — URL hard-coded rather than read from env()
strengths: The only implementation that uses Cache::flexible([60, 300]) (app/Services/TeamDashboard.php:15). This matches the brief exactly: fresh for 60s, stale-while-revalidate up to 5 minutes, and immediate event invalidation on top
Three focused observers implementing ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit. Moves are handled through getPrevious(), and the team is resolved from project_id instead of a cached relation
Variadic TeamDashboard::forget(?int ...$teamIds) with array_unique/array_filter is tidy
Lock plus a double-check inside the lock, a 15s failure cooldown, Http::timeout(3), and a 30-day last-good copy
Tests cover a lock held by another request (with and without last-known rates), the failure cooldown, malformed payloads, 500s, time travel for TTLs, and other teams' caches being left alone

bugs: The dashboard uses a plain Cache::remember with a 5-minute TTL, with no stale-while-revalidate. Every expiry or invalidation leads to a synchronous recompute on the request path, so the 'slightly stale is OK if recomputing is slow' allowance goes unused (app/Dashboard/BuildDashboard.php:23).
A waiter on the refresh lock blocks for up to 5s (block(5)) before returning stale data, which exceeds the 3s slow-API budget (probe: 5.08s).
An API response of {"rates": []} is cached as fresh for an hour and served with stale:false (probe confirmed). is_array accepts an empty array.
antipatterns: routes/api.php:7 — ->middleware(['web','auth']) inside api.php to get session auth; this mixes the web stack into API routes
app/Observers/DashboardCacheObserver.php:33 — private teamIds() has no return type and returns an Eloquent or base collection depending on the branch
app/ExchangeRates/FetchExchangeRates.php:59 — catches the generic RuntimeException thrown by its own throw_unless, a mild control-flow-by-exception pattern
tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:10-14 — Http::swap(new Factory) in a freshHttp() helper to reset fakes, which is ceremony
app/Dashboard/BuildDashboard.php:16-17 — long docblock explaining the design rationale
strengths: Single DashboardCacheObserver attached with #[ObservedBy], implementing ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit. It resolves team ids from project_id plus getPrevious(), so moves invalidate both teams and stale loaded relations aren't a problem
Task saving hook keeps completed_at consistent with status, and reopening clears it
Strong model layer: #[Scope] attributes, enum cast, hasManyThrough for team tasks, sensible composite indexes
Clean invokable action classes and thin controllers; FormRequest normalises case and exposes a typed currency() accessor
Exchange rates: lock with double-check, 30s failure cooldown, last-known copy, Http::timeout(3), report() on failure
Tests use the query log to prove cache hits, time travel for TTLs, and cover both-team invalidation on moves, the failure cooldown and recovery

bugs: Task invalidation reads $model->project?->team_id (app/Observers/DashboardCacheObserver.php:43). If the project relation is already loaded and project_id is then changed directly, the cached old relation is used and the new team's dashboard is never invalidated, leaving it stale for up to 5 minutes. Probe confirmed this. It also lazy-loads a Project on every task save.

GET /api/exchange-rates/{currency} is placed behind web+auth middleware (routes/api.php:7-10). The task does not ask for auth, so unauthenticated clients get 401 (and a non-JSON request gets a 500 because no login route exists).
The dashboard uses a plain Cache::remember with a 5-minute TTL, with no stale-while-revalidate, so the 'serve stale up to 5 minutes' allowance goes unused (app/Dashboard/TeamDashboard.php:26).
Lock waiters block for up to lock_wait=5s before falling back to stale data, which exceeds the 3s budget (probe: 4.94s).
antipatterns: tests/Feature/ExchangeRatesTest.php:13-30 — uses $GLOBALS['rates_api'] to swap fake behaviour between steps, a global-state hack in place of Http::fake sequences or re-faking
routes/api.php:7 — the 'web' middleware group applied to API routes
app/Http/Requests/ExchangeRateRequest.php:17 — regex:/^[A-Z]{3}$/ where alpha:ascii|size:3 is more readable
app/Observers/DashboardCacheObserver.php:44-46 — calls getPrevious() repeatedly with a nested ternary inside the match arm
app/Rates/ExchangeRates.php:35 and :58 — the failed-key check is duplicated before and inside the lock
strengths: Includes a genuine re-entrancy stampede test (a nested call during the API call gets null) and a test asserting the 3-second timeout option
Config-driven timeout, lock wait and backoff values in services.rates
Small private key helpers (freshKey/lastKnownKey/failedKey) and a payload() builder keep ExchangeRates readable
Same strong model layer as impl-2: #[Scope], enum cast, saving hook for completed_at, hasManyThrough, indexes
Observer uses ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit and handles user and project team moves through getPrevious()

v.rationale: All three pass their own suites (impl-1 26, impl-2 29, impl-3 30), and they share a lot of structure. The ranking comes down to how closely each matched the caching brief and to the bugs the probes found. impl-1 is the only one that uses Cache::flexible([60,300]). That is the idiomatic answer to 'reflect changes within seconds, but serving stale data for up to 5 minutes is fine if recomputing is slow', and it combines it with after-commit observer invalidation that resolves teams by project_id. It also has the best stampede tests (a held lock, with and without last-known rates). Its weaknesses are API routes living in web.php (session cookies on API responses), exception-driven control flow around a broad RuntimeException, and no hook keeping completed_at in sync with status. impl-2 has the cleanest model and observer design and a completed_at hook, and its invalidation is correct, including moves. However, it uses plain remember (no stale-while-revalidate), has no lock-contention test, caches an empty rates payload as fresh, and adds 'web' middleware to api.php. impl-3 is almost identical to impl-2 but has a confirmed invalidation bug: it reads the possibly stale loaded $task->project relation, so the new team's dashboard is missed when a task moves. It also puts exchange-rates behind auth for no reason and uses $GLOBALS to swap fakes in its tests, which outweighs its nice timeout and re-entrancy tests. All three let lock waiters block for about 5s, beyond the 3s slow-API budget.
